audiences.name: Solo freelancers preparing client intake
audiences.description: First test: a freelancer who uses Claude or ChatGPT and needs an intake form for an upcoming project or service launch. Disqualify buyers whose existing free form already meets the need, or whose required capabilities remain unverified.

audiences.name: Small agencies managing client forms
audiences.description: Potential trigger: a new client requires a separate intake workflow or branded form. Validate client-workspace billing, guest access and approval requirements before prioritizing this segment.

audiences.name: Organizers launching a paid workshop or event
audiences.description: A focused second test: registration connected to the organizer’s own Stripe account. Disqualify requirements for ticketing, refunds or attendee management until those capabilities are verified.

audiences.name: Sales teams redesigning inbound enquiries
audiences.description: Potential trigger: an existing enquiry process creates manual qualification and follow-up work. Validate the complete response-handling workflow before positioning Formkit as a sales-automation product.

competitors.name: Paperform

Everything else in reach.” Free includes 30 submissions/month and Pro starts at $49/month equivalent billed annually; its no-transaction-fee messaging means Formkit’s no-cut arrangement is not exclusive.

output.positioning:
DECISION — Test client intake for solo freelancers who already use Claude or ChatGPT. Confidence: Low for segment demand; High for the supplied chat-building, free-tier and paid-entry facts.

WORKFLOW TO DEMONSTRATE — Give Claude or ChatGPT a client-intake request → build the form → review it → publish from chat → submit a genuine test enquiry. Chat-based building and publishing are confirmed; this particular end-to-end intake demonstration has not been observed, and no speed, conversion or follow-up benefit is established.

ALTERNATIVE — Email/spreadsheet intake or an existing form builder. These are candidate alternatives, not verified Formkit switching histories; interviews must establish what buyers actually replace.

FRAME — A client-intake form builder, positioned within an existing category. Reject “cheapest forms” because free alternatives exist, and reject “unique AI-chat forms” because Typeform and Jotform also promote MCP access: https://www.typeform.com/mcp and https://www.jotform.com/mcp/.

SWAP TEST — The complete claim combines building and publishing in chat, unlimited free forms and responses, and Pro at $6 per seat monthly. Substituting Typeform or Jotform makes the stated package inaccurate against their supplied entry prices and free limits; the workflow mechanism alone is not unique.

VALUE THEMES — All are Low-confidence Formkit hypotheses, not established customer outcomes.
• “Get intake ready without wrestling with setup.” Four of 21 supplied competitor excerpts concern setup/usability, including “customizing the templates can be a tad cumbersome” and “take a bit of time to fully understand the workflow.” Sources: https://www.capterra.com/p/137289/Typeform/ and https://www.g2.com/products/jotform/reviews?page=4. Demonstrate the workflow rather than claiming Formkit is easier.
• “Keep collecting responses without watching a submission counter.” One of 21 excerpts mentions submission capacity and another describes expensive topping up; this is thin evidence, not a frequency estimate. Sources: https://www.capterra.com/p/158456/JotForm-4-0/reviews/ and https://www.g2.com/products/paperform/reviews. Formkit’s unlimited free responses support the offer, not a claim of unlimited AI processing.
• “Know the paid cost before switching.” Seven of 21 excerpts concern price/value, including “The pricing is the main downside” and “hard to justify the price tag.” Sources: https://www.g2.com/products/typeform/pricing and https://www.g2.com/products/jotform/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons. Show seat totals and allowances, not a blanket savings promise.

MESSAGING — Ready-to-use options; each headline pairs with its numbered subhead.
1. Headline: “Build your next client-intake form in Claude or ChatGPT.”
Subhead: “Use Formkit to build and publish forms directly inside your AI assistant. Start free with unlimited forms and responses.”
2. Headline: “Unlimited forms and responses. Free to start.”
Subhead: “Try Formkit on your next client-intake form, with unlimited members included on Free. Choose a paid plan when it fits your needs.”
3. Headline: “Pro for $6 per seat a month.”
Subhead: “Start with Formkit’s free tier or choose Pro at $6 per seat per month. Yearly billing gives you two months free.”

PILLARS WITH PROOF — “Build and publish where you already chat”: confirmed Claude and ChatGPT compatibility. “Collect responses without a free-plan submission cap”: confirmed unlimited forms, responses and members. “See the paid entry price clearly”: confirmed Pro and Business per-seat prices; do not attach unverified entitlements to either plan.

WORDS TO USE — Client intake, questions, responses, workflow, build and publish, per seat. WORDS TO AVOID — Unlimited AI, unique MCP, cheapest, effortless, guaranteed conversions, replaces your team.

PITCH ORDER — 1. Show the freelancer’s intake task. 2. Acknowledge email and existing forms as valid alternatives. 3. Set buying criteria: publishing workflow, response capacity and total cost. 4. Show the actual chat-to-published-form recording. 5. Explain Free, paid-seat pricing and verified limits. 6. Ask the visitor to build their next intake form.

VALIDATION — Proposed window: October 19–November 29, 2026. Start with 12 buyer interviews, then test the focused page against the current page; do not call the position validated from competitor language or a small ad sample.
output.pricingNotes: Pro is $6/seat/month and Business $19; yearly options offer two months free. The supplied research explicitly gives three Pro seats as $18/month, versus Fillout’s advertised $15/month entry with unlimited seats; features and billing commitments differ: https://www.fillout.com/pricing. Formkit’s free tier is not unique against Tally, and no-cut Stripe payments are not exclusive against Paperform: https://tally.so/ and https://paperform.co/pricing/. Do not publish AI-response allowances or plan-specific payment entitlements until confirmed; unlimited submissions must not imply unlimited AI processing.

Primary metric: buyers independently showing the same problem and a paid-capability need; stop after 12 interviews and proceed only if at least eight demonstrate that pattern, otherwise revise the segment.

Cap exploration at $300, pause a keyword group after $75 without a published form, and stop for review at the cap; do not rank groups on payment economics below 10 paid workspaces each or exceed $600 in any month.

output.positioningStatement: For solo freelancers preparing client intake, Formkit lets you build and publish your form inside Claude or ChatGPT, start with unlimited forms and responses free, and choose Pro at $6 per seat per month.
output.confidenceNotes:
EVIDENCE DATE — Supplied research was captured October 18, 2026; no fresh browsing or customer interviews were performed in this drafting pass. Proposed validation dates run October 19, 2026–January 10, 2027, within the requested 90-day horizon.

POOLS — Thin bank: 21 competitor-review excerpts across nine cited pages on two review platforms; Formkit-user pool N=0 and forum pool N=0. Unique-review totals, review dates, deduplication and authenticity checks are unavailable; excerpts are not necessarily independent reviews.

COUNTS — Within the competitor-excerpt pool only: price/value 7/21 across six pages; setup/usability 4/21 across four; respondent experience/reliability 3/21 across two; layout/customization 2/21 across two; reporting/exports 2/21 across two; submission capacity, support and languages each 1/21 on one page. These are coding counts, not complaint prevalence; intensity was not scored, and all remain signals rather than validated findings.

PHRASE GROUPS — Problem and objection groups contain verbatim supplied excerpts. Trigger, outcome and proof groups remain empty because no qualifying quotations were supplied; no phrase is verified as repeated high-confidence language, and no Formkit site copy is treated as customer voice.

CONFIDENCE BY COMPONENT — High: supplied confirmed Formkit product/pricing facts and identified evidence limits. Medium: competitor offer observations as of the research date and review-language signals. Low: segment priority, buyer triggers, value themes, conversion journey, workflow advantage, positioning demand and channel economics; the messaging uses confirmed claims but its effectiveness is untested.

NOT ACCESSED — No forum threads or Formkit-user sources were supplied or accessed in this pass; no login barrier is being inferred. Live competitor prices, ad libraries, rankings and social activity were not rechecked, so the report makes no current channel-absence, ad-spend or performance claim.

EXPERIMENT LIMITS — Budgets, dates, minimum volumes and decision thresholds are proposed operating assumptions, not benchmarks or forecasts. Volume thresholds may not be reachable on this budget; stop at the stated cap or date, report inconclusive results when necessary, and never increase spend merely to reach a sample target.

v22.topIssue: The report hedges so heavily that it buries the plan. It downgrades every audience to low confidence and spends weeks on interviews and sample thresholds likely unreachable on $600/month. A non-expert owner trying to get paying customers within 90 days gets caveats and jargon (MCP, swap test, paid workspaces per visitor) instead of a clear, confident path to revenue.

Uses forms for primary attendee or vendor intake: observe application links and registration instructions; distinguishes a relevant workflow from a secondary scholarship-only form.
disqualifiers: Exclude existing customers, competitors, competitor partners and suppressed contacts; customer and suppression inputs were not provided.
Exclude closed operations, unusable websites or purchasing confirmed to be controlled elsewhere; verify these before outreach.
Exclude secondary-only form use; block ineligible jurisdictions and addresses, including the supplied organizational Gmail addresses.
Disposition: 9 candidates, 1 exclusion for secondary-only intake; 8 source-refresh holds and 1 jurisdiction-plus-refresh hold. All 9 also require customer and suppression checks.

triggers: Application launch or announced form migration: creates a deadline to choose and publish the intake process; observe dated application announcements.
Market-season opening or scheduled paid workshop: creates registration and payment work; observe season dates and registration instructions, without assuming dissatisfaction.
Nice-to-have: multiple simultaneous application cycles; observe calendars and application links, because unlimited forms can support separate event intake.
Nice-to-have: existing Stripe use; observe payment instructions, because it would reduce payment-provider change. No prospect’s Stripe use is confirmed.

sequence.purpose: Step 1, variant A (payment pain): one sourced observation, the mechanism (form and payment together through the prospect's own Stripe account, no cut), the free plan, and a one-word-answer ask.

sequence.subject: build forms from chat
sequence.body: One more way in: Formkit works with Claude and ChatGPT, so you can ask the assistant to build and publish a form from the chat without opening a builder. Or you describe the form in plain words and Formkit's AI builds it. Want a sample vendor application to start from?
sequence.purpose: New angle: AI-built forms and the Claude and ChatGPT route, with the same easy ask. No plan limits claimed.

sequence.subject: application outline offer
sequence.body: If useful, I can write a one-page outline of how I'd set your application up as one form: the questions, the logic that sends each applicant down the right path, and where payment fits. Want it? For reference, paid plans are Pro at $6 a seat a month and Business at $19.
sequence.purpose: Rung 2 resource, offered without a link and tied to their form, plus the confirmed paid prices as a new fact.

sequence.subject: leaving it here
sequence.body: I'll leave it here. If vendor applications or registrations get harder to juggle, reply and I'll send the sample form. Yearly billing on paid plans gets two months free, and the free plan has unlimited forms, responses and members.
sequence.purpose: Polite close-out with no link and no pressure, restating only confirmed offer terms.

v22.topIssue: The prospect list is mostly volunteer-run band boosters, cheer associations and tiny markets, which are unlikely to pay. The emails pitch the free plan while implying that Stripe payments come with it, so the work misses the goal of paying customers and blurs which plan delivers the payment feature. Every prospect is also left on hold, with no named contact or email address, so the owner cannot actually start the outreach.
